basis.en: Public domain: the artist died in 1916. The Metropolitan Museum of Art releases this image under CC0 through its Open Access programme.
basis.zh: 公有领域：作者卒于 1916 年。大都会艺术博物馆通过开放获取计划以 CC0 发布此图像。

alt.en: Two elderly men sit over a chessboard in a dim, panelled parlour, each with a hand raised to his face, while a third man stands behind the board watching. Glasses and a decanter of wine stand on a small table at the left, a clock sits on the mantel, and a cat rests on the red carpet.
alt.zh: 一间昏暗、镶着护墙板的客厅里，两位老人对着棋盘坐着，各自把一只手抬到脸边，第三个人站在棋盘后面观看。左边的小桌上放着酒杯和一只盛酒的玻璃瓶，壁炉台上有一座钟，一只猫卧在红地毯上。

note.en: Eakins painted this small panel in 1876 and gave it to the Met five years later; the standing man is usually identified as the painter’s father, Benjamin Eakins, watching two friends play. It is a careful picture of thinking, in which nothing moves but attention. Forty years earlier Poe had argued that this kind of thinking could not be done by clockwork, so a person had to be hiding inside Maelzel’s chess-playing automaton.
note.zh: 伊肯斯 1876 年画了这块小木板，五年后把它送给了大都会艺术博物馆；站着的人通常被认为是画家的父亲本杰明·伊肯斯，正看着两位朋友下棋。这是一幅细致描绘思考的画，除了注意力，什么都没有在动。早在四十年前，爱伦·坡就论证过，这样的思考不可能由机械完成，所以梅尔策尔那台下棋自动机里一定藏着一个人。
